the epsilon subunit is a light-activated ATP synthase inhibitor, that the carboxyl-terminus of epsilon is exposed in illuminated membranes, that the epsilon sub unit can be stripped from the ATP synthas e in illuminated membranes by antibodies against the carboxyl termini of the epsilon sub unit, and that the epsilon subunits stripped from the ATPase are inactive.

the mechanism of ATP synthesis in chloroplasts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the epsilon subunit is a conformational sensor of the electrochemical proton potential and that the carboxyl-terminus of the epsilon is exposed in the active state of the ATP synthase.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that a portion of the epsilon subunits is exposed on the surface of the ATP synthase during illumination.
the ATP synthase is activated by the proton gradient and that the epsilon subunit is the component that senses the proton gradient and transmits that information to the catalytic site.
the carboxyl termini of the epsilon subunits of the chloroplast and mitochondrial ATP synthases are exposed during illumination of chloroplasts and mitochondria, respectively.

the carboxyl termini of the epsilon subunits are solvent exposed during the ATP synthase activation by the proton gradient.
